name: PV
description: PV returns the current value of a future stream of cash flows discounted at a constant rate.
tldr: Calculates the present value of a series of future payments or a future lump sum.

parameters.name: fv
parameters.description: Future value or cash balance after the last payment (default 0).

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: 0 = end of period (default), 1 = beginning of period.

basicExample.explanation: The value today of receiving $1,000 per month for 30 years at 5% annual interest.

advancedExamples.title: Present value of a future goal
advancedExamples.description: How much do I need today to have $50,000 in 10 years at 7%?
advancedExamples.explanation: You need $25,417 today to grow to $50,000 in 10 years at 7% interest.

howItWorks: PV discounts each future cash flow back to today using the discount rate. The result is positive when future payments are entered as negative outflows.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: All inputs must use the same period unit.
Assumes constant payments and a constant discount rate.
Does not account for inflation, taxes, or fees.

commonErrors.cause: The rate was not adjusted for the period.
commonErrors.fix: Divide annual rate by the number of periods per year.

commonErrors.cause: Future value or payments have the wrong sign.
commonErrors.fix: Use negative for outflows and positive for inflows.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: PV works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the present value formula?
faq.answer: PV = FV / (1 + r)^n, where r is the rate and n is the number of periods.

faq.question: Can PV calculate a perpetuity?
faq.answer: Excel PV does not directly support infinite cash flows, but a perpetuity equals payment divided by rate.

faq.question: Why is PV negative?
faq.answer: PV is positive when future payments are negative. The sign follows cash-flow convention.
